short: English novelist whose social realism and biting irony defined the Georgian novel of manners.
full:
Jane Austen lived most of her life within a close-knit family on the fringes of the English country gentry, an environment that provided the intensely focused social canvas for her fiction. Publishing anonymously during her lifetime, her major works, including Sense and Sensibility and Pride and Prejudice, offered brilliant, unsentimental dissections of the economic realities of marriage for women of her class.

Although her novels gained only modest success while she lived, their sharp psychological insight and pioneering use of free indirect discourse exerted a profound influence on the development of the English novel. Today, she is widely recognised as a master of prose fiction whose works endure for their wit, structural perfection, and enduring social critique.
